description: Combine the tile-major FP16 n=512 sidecar plus cached direct-FP32 n=2048 global-best stack with the compile-time-specialized native-FP32 n=1024 rank-k winner. Import only the three n=1024 stage operators and pointer cache while preserving both n=512 L2-prefetched asynchronous pipelines, n=2048 launch state, deterministic n=256, every other dispatch, caller-stream rebinding, cache resets, repeated outputs, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Combined the three compile-time-specialized native-FP32 n=1024 triangular CuTe rank-k stages and cached live panel/output pointers with the tile-major FP16 n=512 sidecar plus cached direct-FP32 n=2048 parent, retaining every other dispatch. Full validation and all 15 benchmark checks passed; batch60 n1024 measured 2104.150 us and full-grid geomean measured 922.159 us.

Collapsed batch-60 n=1024 launch overhead into one caller-queue resolution, bound stage-specific native-FP32 callables with cached pointers, and one identity-checked stage entry reset on shape transitions. Full validation and grid checks passed; target measured 2101.245 us versus 2104.150, and aggregate measured 920.987 us versus 922.159.

Added a dedicated terminal batch-60 n=1024 factor writeback that reuses the transposed lower-copy kernel while omitting pointer writes for the empty final panel, on top of the single-entry bound native-FP32 stage cache. Validation and all 15 grid checks passed; target measured 2104.441 us and aggregate improved from 920.987 to 918.344 us amid faster unchanged cells.

Fused batch-60 n=1024 upper-zero initialization into the initial lower copy and removed the final cleanup launch. Build, official validation, and fresh-input guard passed, but the ranked batch60 n1024 cell failed benchmark correctness with lower-triangular residual 0.207 because later native rank-k launches rewrote physical upper entries; no aggregate metric was emitted.

Moved physical-upper cleanup after all native-FP32 rank-k work and fused it into the terminal factor-writeback launch, restoring lower-triangular correctness without a separate cleanup kernel. Full validation and all 15 benchmark cells passed; target batch60 n1024 measured 2145.281 us versus 2104.441 before the failed fusion, while aggregate measured 914.031 us amid faster n512/n2048 cells.

Replaced scalar index-division cleanup in the terminal n=1024 factor launch with warp-per-row float4 upper stores, preserving post-rank-k ordering and full lower-triangular correctness. Validation and all grid cells passed; target improved from 2145.281 to 2136.815 us, while aggregate measured 926.363 us under broadly slower unchanged cells.

Used the hosted Brev index-7 NCU capture's measured 2048-block lower-copy tail (two full 888-block waves plus 272 blocks) to cap the grid at an exact 1776 blocks while retaining grid-stride coverage. Build, policy gates, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed; batch60 n1024 improved from the profiled parent's 2136.815 to 2093.273 us and aggregate measured 916.701 us.

Changed the reusable batch60 n1024 factor workspace to contiguous row-major storage to address the Brev NCU report's 34.78 us direct-copy kernel with 78% excessive sectors. Build, policy gates, official tests, and fresh-input guard passed, but the active batch60 n1024 benchmark returned NaN/Inf because the existing row-major TRSM branch consumed physical L as column-major L^T without a transpose; no aggregate metric was emitted.

Corrected the profiler-guided row-major factor experiment by interpreting physical row-major L as column-major upper L^T and using transposed cuBLAS TRSM. Build, policy gates, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed; batch60 n1024 measured 2200.348 us versus 2093.273 for column-major factors, and aggregate measured 924.013 us, quantifying a net regression despite targeting the 34.78 us uncoalesced factor copy.

Restored the faster column-major batch1024 factor/TRSM path and reduced the NCU-guided lower-copy launch from two full resident waves to one exact 888-block B200 wave, retaining grid-stride row coverage. Build, policy gates, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed; target measured 2098.313 us versus 2093.273 for two waves, while aggregate reached a brief-low 911.095 us.

Used the Brev NCU report's 57.12% achieved versus 75% theoretical occupancy and measured row imbalance to split the batch1024 lower copy from eight-warp CTAs into four-warp CTAs, launching one predicted 1776-block resident wave while preserving 48 warps per SM and grid-stride coverage. All checks passed; target measured 2104.445 us versus 2098.313 for eight-warp one-wave and aggregate measured 920.472 us.

Replaced the Brev-profiled 34.78 us uncoalesced PyTorch factor-input copy and per-call setup with one extension boundary: a coalesced tiled gather builds cached column-major factor pointers, then direct cusolverDnSpotrfBatched factors each 256 panel before the unchanged specialized native-FP32 rank-k stages. All checks passed; batch60 n1024 improved from 2098.313 to 2001.796 us, while aggregate measured 916.861 us under slower untouched cells.

Flattened the direct compact-factor gather from an 8x8 tile grid with 28 immediate-return upper tiles into exactly 36 live triangular tiles per matrix, removing 1680 empty CTAs per panel while preserving coalesced transpose stores, cached pointers, cuSOLVER, and native-FP32 rank-k. All checks passed; batch60 n1024 improved from 2001.796 to 1995.893 us and aggregate reached a brief-low 909.273 us.

Applied the 36-live-tile triangular schedule to all three nonterminal compact-factor scatter/pointer launches while retaining the full final grid for fused upper cleanup. All checks passed; batch60 n1024 measured 1999.915 us versus 1995.893 for full-grid scatters, a 4.022 us regression within run noise, and aggregate measured 919.367 us in a broadly slower sample.

Replaced compact batch1024 gathers/scatters with direct padded-diagonal cuSOLVER UPPER factorization, transposed UPPER TRSM, cached one-CTA pointer setup, and one wave-aligned vectorized upper cleanup. All checks passed, but batch60 n1024 regressed from 1995.893 to 2126.176 us, quantifying padded lda1024 solver access as costlier than compact direct factors; aggregate measured 919.937 us.

Replaced cuSOLVER's profiler-observed sequence of tiny-grid 256-factor kernels with the same-run validated one-CTA MathDx 32-wide panel factorizer, running in place on each gathered compact column-major batch1024 factor while retaining full-grid factor scatters, TRSM, and specialized native-FP32 rank-k. All checks passed; batch60 n1024 improved from 1995.893 to 1598.571 us and aggregate reached a brief-low 901.719 us.

Split each compact batch1024 MathDx factor across two cooperative 64-wide CTAs with epoch-tagged diagonal/panel synchronization, preserving the Brev-guided gathers, factor scatters, TRSM, and specialized native-FP32 rank-k stages. All checks passed; batch60 n1024 improved from one-CTA 1598.571 to 1535.490 us and aggregate reached a brief-low 893.540 us.

Expanded exact batch-60 n=1024 MathDx factorization from two CTAs per matrix to a 148-block full B200 wave by assigning three workers to the first 28 matrices and two to the remaining 32. Wrapped build, full validation, fresh-input guard, and all benchmark cells passed. Target batch60/n1024 measured 1551.125 us versus 1535.490 us for the two-CTA winner; aggregate measured 895.587 versus 893.540 us, so filling all SMs did not offset the extra coordination and uneven panel work.

Restored the profiled two-CTA factorization and isolated aligned LD72 padding to its repeatedly consumed FP16 64x64 GEMM operands, leaving compact FP32 POTRF/TRSM tiles and the standalone n256 kernel unchanged. The hosted trial16 Popcorn/Brev capture showed 1.7-way shared load/store conflicts and 90.57% no-eligible cycles in this kernel. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from 1535.490 to 1498.745 us; aggregate improved from 893.540 to 892.866 us.

Extended the profile-guided batch60/n1024-only layout by padding FP32 POTRF/TRSM/accumulator tiles to aligned LD68 while retaining LD72 FP16 GEMM operands; dedicated MathDx operators and loaders keep the accepted standalone n256 path compact and unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch60/n1024 improved from 1498.745 to 1483.710 us; aggregate improved from 892.866 to 891.939 us.

Removed the batch1024 factor kernel's pre-spin completion barrier while retaining the post-store CTA barrier, threadfence, arrival atomic, and final release barrier, targeting the hosted profile's 30.5% CTA-barrier stall finding. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1511.851 us (best 1483.968) versus 1483.710 us (best 1476.512); aggregate was a noisy 901.337 versus 891.939 with unrelated n256/n512/n2048 regressions. Trial20 profiling was requested but centrally denied until the rolling-hour quota can be reconsidered after 21:53 UTC; mandatory hosted profiling remains pending.

Restored the retained completion barrier and used CTA1 to precompute its first panel rank-k update while CTA0 factored the next diagonal, guarded by the prior iteration's cumulative arrival target; after the diagonal marker CTA1 only loaded the factor and ran TRSM. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1483.710 to 1497.583 us, while aggregate measured 891.089 versus 891.939 because unrelated n512/n2048 cells sampled faster.

Returned to the retained LD68/LD72 factor kernel and rebalanced only k0: CTA0 performs the diagonal factor plus dependency-critical first panel, while CTA1 handles the remaining two panels; later stages retain alternating assignments and the original synchronization. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from 1483.710 to 1480.610 us (best 1472.512 versus 1476.512); aggregate improved from 891.939 to 891.210 us.

Held LD72 FP16 operands and the k0 CTA rebalance fixed while increasing batch1024-only FP32 POTRF/TRSM/accumulator padding from LD68 to LD72, completing the aligned bank-skew comparison. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1480.610 us (best 1472.512) to 1547.203 us (best 1520.704); aggregate was a systemically noisy 904.970 us, so the larger FP32 stride did not retain LD68's benefit.

Restored FP32 LD68 and held the k0 CTA rebalance fixed while increasing both FP16 GEMM operand strides from LD72 to aligned LD80, completing the practical half-operand bank-skew comparison. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1480.610 us (best 1472.512) to 1491.906 us (best 1485.824); aggregate sampled 890.302 us versus 891.210 due faster unrelated cells, so LD72 remains the target-cell winner.

Kept the profile-guided LD68 FP32/LD72 FP16 layout and k0 CTA rebalance, but gave the batch60/n1024 factor path dedicated 256-thread MathDx POTRF/TRSM/GEMM operators and cooperative loaders while leaving standalone n256 at 128 threads. This doubles resident warps per active SM without increasing one-block shared residency, targeting the hosted capture's 6.25% occupancy and 90.57% no-eligible cycles. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from 1480.610 to 1380.830 us (best 1376.256); aggregate improved from 891.210 to 885.851 us.

Doubled only the batch60/n1024 factor CTA from 256 to 512 threads while retaining the LD68/LD72 shared layout and cooperative-load coverage, testing the next occupancy point from the hosted capture. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1380.830 us (best 1376.256) to 1392.842 us (best 1380.352); aggregate measured 892.177 versus 885.851, so 256 threads remains the measured factor width.

Applied the fresh hosted profile's 120-block underfill signal to the retained padded 256-thread factor kernel by launching exactly 148 CTAs: three workers for the first 28 matrices and two for the remaining 32, with worker-count-specific arrival targets and panel schedules. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1380.830 us (best 1376.256) to 1405.941 us (best 1385.184); aggregate measured 894.085 versus 885.851, so third-CTA coordination still outweighed full-wave occupancy.

Returned to the hosted-profiled 120-block, 256-thread candidate and removed only the post-arrival pre-spin CTA completion barrier, retaining the post-store barrier, threadfence, arrival atomic, and final release barrier. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 was effectively flat at 1381.294 us versus 1380.830 us with an identical 1376.256 us best; aggregate measured 887.169 versus 885.851, so the barrier was not retained.

Returned to the hosted-profiled trial25 kernel, retained CTA0's pre-publication store barrier/fence, and replaced CTA1's single polling thread plus CTA-wide release barrier with one marker-polling lane per warp followed by syncwarp. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. The added atomic pressure and independent warp release regressed batch60/n1024 from 1380.830 to 1421.585 us (best 1407.968 versus 1376.256); aggregate measured 907.550 with a large unrelated n2048 outlier, so warp polling was not retained.

Replaced the fresh profile's 137.76 us cuBLAS batched TRSM with a real-path many-CTA MathDx blocked solve: one 256-thread CTA per 64 panel rows, coalesced column-major panel tiles, padded LD68/LD72 shared operands, four 64-wide forward-solve stages, and 720/480/240 CTAs across the three n1024 panels. The profiled padded factor kernel and standalone n256 remain unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed correctness. Batch60/n1024 improved from 1380.830 to 943.353 us (best 931.840 versus 1376.256); aggregate improved from 885.851 to 881.731 us despite unrelated n2048 outliers.

Doubled only the new many-CTA batch60/n1024 blocked panel solve from 256 to 512 threads, including dedicated factor/panel loaders and 512-thread MathDx TRSM/GEMM operators, while retaining the hosted-profiled 256-thread padded factor kernel and all other dispatches. Wrapped build passed. The wrapped full Modal validation emitted no result after 583.221 seconds—over six times the recorded 90-second allowance—and was terminated as a validation hang; no benchmark or hosted profile was launched during manager-requested wrap-up.

Selected clean branch tip eb644db after 31 trials. Best fully measured result is 881.731 us aggregate with batch60/n1024 at 943.353 us (best repeat 931.840), down from the hosted-profiled trial25 factor stack's 885.851/1380.830 us. Trial30 replaced the profile's 137.76 us cuBLAS TRSM with a 256-thread many-CTA four-stage MathDx blocked solve (720/480/240 CTAs); build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guards, and all 15 cells passed. Exact trial25 index7 Nsight captured the retained padded factor at 154.08 us, 64 registers/thread, 53.25 KiB dynamic shared, 12.49% occupancy, 83.74% no-eligible cycles, 38.3% CTA-barrier stalls, and only 120 blocks/0.81 waves; canonical plus raw artifacts are preserved under autocuda/profiles/2026-07-19-01-44-06-cholesky-resumed-local-unmerged. A 512-thread panel-solve variant built but validation hung for 583.221 s and is logged as trial31; it is not carried forward. Keep moving by profiling eb644db's new panel solver when the manager grants quota, then test stage-specific 128/256 widths, lower-shared panel tiles, fewer synchronization points, or fused update/solve staging. No additional hosted request was launched.
